facts.fact: The World Bank completion report says construction of five fibre-optic links in Mauritania was under way when the project closing date was extended on 2019-10-20 to allow completion of the fibre backbone links, after delays in signing the construction contract.

The World Bank says five fibre-optic links totalling 1,710 km were laid and became operational under WARCIP APL2, distributing international connectivity from the ACE landing to most provincial capitals and to the Mali, Niger, Burkina Faso and Morocco cross-border links; operators expanded 4G once the links were operational. Date taken as the project closing, 2021-11, the report (2022-08-26) giving no lighting date.

The World Bank says the backbone was built under a PPP and open-access model giving operators fair access to the infrastructure, with state vehicle SDIN established and an affermage contract with IMT signed; no named buyers of capacity are given. No event date is given, so the report's published date is used.

systems.owner: SDIN (state vehicle), operated by IMT under affermage

systems.system: National/regional IXP, carrier hotel and data center
